_about: Grounding corpus for POST /predict precautions and the Module E assistant. Keyed by the model's class label (PlantVillage folder name). Guidance compiled from ICAR / State Agricultural University package-of-practices and university extension pages; confirm chemical choices and doses locally.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves turn yellow and drop early; fruit becomes cracked and corky.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic: Rake and destroy fallen leaves; prune for airflow; apply sulphur or a Bacillus subtilis spray from bud-break at 7-10 day intervals in wet weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical: Protectant sprays of mancozeb or captan before rain; myclobutanil or difenoconazole if scab is already active.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Grow resistant varieties, wide spacing, avoid overhead irrigation, autumn leaf clean-up.
precautions: Spray protectant fungicide before wet spells

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered 'frog-eye' leaf spots; brown, concentric-ringed rot on fruit; cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.organic: Prune out cankers and mummified fruit 30 cm below symptoms; copper sprays; orchard sanitation.
Apple___Black_rot.chemical: Captan or thiophanate-methyl from petal fall through summer.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove deadwood and mummies in winter, manage insect wounds, keep trees vigorous but not over-fertilised.
precautions: Cut out cankered wood well below the lesion
Pick off and destroy mummified fruit

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease signs - uniform green leaves, clean fruit.
Apple___healthy.organic: Maintain balanced nutrition and mulch; scout weekly.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Keep up sanitation, airflow pruning and a preventive spray calendar in wet regions.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces; heavy infection dries leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic: Usually not needed on field maize; on sweet corn use sulphur; grow resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical: Azoxystrobin or propiconazole if rust appears before tasselling on a susceptible hybrid.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Resistant hybrids, timely sowing to escape cool humid spells, balanced nitrogen.
precautions: Spray only if pustules appear before tasselling

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-to-tan lesions running parallel to the veins; lower leaves blight first.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.organic: Rotate away from maize for a year, plough down residue, resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.chemical: Strobilurin + triazole mix (e.g. azoxystrobin + propiconazole) at early lesion stage, around tasselling.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Crop rotation, residue management (main inoculum source), resistant hybrids, avoid dense stands.
precautions: Rotate out of maize for a season

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves uniformly green, no lesions or pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.organic: Maintain balanced NPK and weed control.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Rotation and residue management keep leaf diseases away.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan leaf spots with dark pycnidia dots; young berries rot, shrivel and become hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.organic: Remove mummies and infected tendrils; open the canopy; copper or sulphur sprays from early shoot growth.
Grape___Black_rot.chemical: Mancozeb or myclobutanil from 2-3 leaf stage through to 4-5 weeks after bloom.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Winter sanitation of mummies, canopy management for fast drying, avoid overhead irrigation.
precautions: Strip out and destroy berry mummies
Begin fungicide at early shoot growth
Protect through the pre-bloom to post-bloom window

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Clean green leaves, sound fruit clusters.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Keep the fruit zone open and dry; remove mummies in winter.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots turning brown with yellow halos; scabby raised spots on fruit; leaf drop.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.organic: Use certified clean seed, hot-water seed treatment, copper + mancozeb sprays, remove infected plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical: Copper hydroxide tank-mixed with mancozeb weekly in warm wet weather; rotate with Actigard where available.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Disease-free transplants, 2-3 year rotation, avoid working plants when wet, drip not overhead irrigation.
precautions: Do not handle plants when leaves are wet
Spray copper + mancozeb weekly in wet heat

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Deep green leaves, smooth glossy fruit.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Clean seed and rotation prevent bacterial spot.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric 'target' rings on older lower leaves, surrounded by yellowing; spreads upward.
Potato___Early_blight.organic: Remove lower affected leaves, mulch to stop soil splash, spray Bacillus subtilis or copper; keep plants well fed.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical: Mancozeb or chlorothalonil every 7-10 days from first spots; alternate with azoxystrobin.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Long rotation, certified seed, adequate nitrogen and potassium, avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly spreading water-soaked grey-green blotches on leaf tips/margins, white mould on the underside in humid weather; brown firm tuber rot.
Potato___Late_blight.organic: Destroy volunteers and cull piles; hill soil over tubers; act fast - organic options are weak once established.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical: Protectant mancozeb before disease; on outbreak use cymoxanil+mancozeb, dimethomorph or cyazofamid on a 5-7 day schedule.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Certified seed, resistant varieties, wide spacing, destroy cull piles, spray ahead of cool wet forecasts.
precautions: Act immediately - this disease moves fast
Spray a systemic (cymoxanil/dimethomorph) on a 5-7 day cycle
Destroy infected plants and cull piles

Potato___healthy.chemical: None needed; keep a protectant schedule if late blight is around.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed
Keep a protectant spray ready if late blight is in the area

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Numerous small dark greasy spots on leaves with yellow halos; leaves scorch and drop; raised scabby spots on green fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic: Clean seed / hot-water treatment, copper + mancozeb, remove infected debris, avoid handling wet plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.chemical: Copper hydroxide + mancozeb weekly; add Actigard (acibenzolar) in rotation where registered.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Certified transplants, 2-3 year rotation, drip irrigation, staking for airflow.
precautions: Never prune or tie plants when wet
Spray copper + mancozeb weekly in warm wet spells
Remove and bag severely spotted plants

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown target-ring spots on the oldest leaves first, yellow margins, lower-leaf defoliation; dark leathery lesions at the stem end of fruit.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic: Strip lower affected leaves, mulch, stake for airflow, spray copper or Bacillus subtilis every 7-10 days.
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb preventively; azoxystrobin or difenoconazole on active disease.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotation, mulching, resistant varieties, balanced nitrogen, drip irrigation.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green blotches on leaves and stems, white downy growth underneath in humid weather; firm brown patches on fruit. Collapses a crop within days.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic: Remove and bag infected plants immediately; organic control is limited once established.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical: Protectant mancozeb/chlorothalonil ahead of cool wet weather; on outbreak use cymoxanil+mancozeb, dimethomorph or cyazofamid every 5-7 days.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties, wide spacing, drip irrigation, destroy nearby volunteer tomato/potato, spray ahead of wet forecasts.
precautions: Act now - late blight destroys crops in days
Check the weather panel and spray before wet spells

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on the upper leaf surface with olive-green to grey velvety mould underneath; mainly a greenhouse/polyhouse problem.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic: Increase ventilation, reduce humidity below 85%, wider spacing, remove lower leaves, copper or Bacillus sprays.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or difenoconazole; rotate modes of action.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Ventilate and heat polyhouses to avoid dew, resistant varieties, avoid leaf wetness, wide spacing.
precautions: Ventilate the polyhouse to drop humidity
Space and prune plants for airflow

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Even green leaves, no spots or mould, healthy growing tips.
Tomato___healthy.organic: Mulch, drip irrigation, staking, weekly scouting.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Rotation, resistant varieties, airflow and dry foliage keep most tomato diseases out.
precautions: Leaf looks healthy - no treatment needed
Keep scouting weekly, especially after rain
